Demand that already exists A(H5) bird flu has been causing outbreaks in U.S. dairy cows, with 71 human cases reported since February 2024 — new subtypes keep crossing over while detection still waits on a laboratory pathway (

Modular recognition unit Keeping the α-factor secretion anchor and linker scaffold and swapping only the VHH sequence would extend coverage toward H5, H7 and other subtypes, while the downstream GPCR signal rewiring and the dual-mode

GPCR signal rewiring and the dual-mode reporter stay universal. Field-ready readout Paired with a low-cost portable fluorescence reader, the same platform could serve primary-care screening, school morning checks and border quarantine ports. PAGER-Yeast is designed to be antigen-agnostic: swap the recognition unit and

-agnostic: swap the recognition unit and the signal readout stays the same. The H1N1 prototype is the first instance of a platform rather than a single-purpose test — the same yeast, the same reporter, one new nanobody at a time. Explore Our Wiki Design Results Model Human Practices

GER 可编程抗原门控受体技术将 HA 抗原识别事件转化为绿色荧光信号，构建低成本、高灵敏度的 POCT 生物传感器。 项目背景与动机 问题与潜在影响 流感作为全球重大公共卫生威胁，快速、准确的现场筛查是控制疫情传播的关键环节。现有临床检测方法存在以下局限： qRT-PCR：高准确度，但成本高、依赖专业实验设备、检测周期长，难以满足基层与现场需求。 ELISA：可高通量检测，但灵敏度偏低、孵育步骤复杂，对操作环境要求较高。 胶体金试纸条：操作简便、现场快速，但只能定性判读，低病毒载量样本易漏检。 上述方法在成本控制、灵敏度与便携性之间存在难以兼顾的矛盾，迫切需要开发一种低成本、高灵敏度、可现场部署的新型检测平台。 项目目标 本项目核

迫切需要开发一种低成本、高灵敏度、可现场部署的新型检测平台。 项目目标 本项目核心目标为：将 PAGER（Protein-fragment Assisted Interaction Reporter）可编程抗原门控受体技术应用于酿酒酵母，构建膜表面抗原识别融合蛋白，实现甲型流感病毒 HA 抗原的快速可视化检测。 当样本中存在 IAV HA 抗原时，酵母细胞表面的纳米抗体捕获抗原，通过空间位阻解除受体自抑制，在 DCZ 激动剂存在下激活下游 G 蛋白信号通路，驱动 FUS1 启动子表达 yEGFP/lacZ 报告基因，发出绿色荧光或蓝色显色信号，实现"抗原结合—荧光发光"的直接转换。 为何选择此项目 选择酿酒酵母作为生物传感器底盘基于

结合—荧光发光"的直接转换。 为何选择此项目 选择酿酒酵母作为生物传感器底盘基于以下考量：BY4741 遗传背景清晰、分子操作成熟、培养条件简单、生物安全等级为 BSL-1，适合规模化发酵生产。PAGER 系统将抗原识别与受体激活解耦，仅通过替换纳米抗体即可拓展至其他病原体检测，具有高度的模块化与可扩展性。 执行摘要：PAGER 策略通过"MT1 抑制肽—hM1Dq 受体—anti-HA 纳米抗体"三元嵌合设计实现抗原门控：无 HA 时通路关闭，有 HA 时空间位阻解除抑制并激活双模式报告系统。 核心设计思路：PAGER策略 抗原门控受体原理 PAGER（Protein-fragment Assisted Interaction R

（Protein-fragment Assisted Interaction Reporter，蛋白片段辅助互作报告系统）是一种基于空间位阻调控的可编程抗原门控受体策略。其核心是将抑制肽、抗原识别纳米抗体与 G 蛋白偶联受体（GPCR）整合为单一膜融合蛋白。 PAGER 膜融合蛋白结构（N→C 端） α-factor 信号肽 (GGGS)₃ MT1 抑制肽 (GGGS)₃ anti-HA 纳米抗体 (GGGS)₃ TEVcs Linker hM1Dq 受体 完整组装结构：α-factor-(GGGS)₃-MT1-(GGGS)₃-anti-HA-TEVcs-hM1Dq。柔性 (GGGS)₃ 接头作为空间延长臂，确保纳米抗体能够穿透酵母

-hM1Dq。柔性 (GGGS)₃ 接头作为空间延长臂，确保纳米抗体能够穿透酵母细胞壁孔隙并接触病毒颗粒抗原。 1 静息关闭状态 无 IAV HA 抗原时，MT1 抑制肽持续占据 hM1Dq 受体的正构位点，下游 G 蛋白级联被钳制在"关闭"状态，无荧光信号产生。 → 2 抗原识别与位阻解锁 HA 抗原与膜表面 anti-HA 纳米抗体结合，产生的空间位阻将 MT1 抑制肽从 hM1Dq 结合口袋中物理位移，解除自抑制。 → 3 DCZ 激活与信号输出 DCZ 小分子激动剂激活 hM1Dq，Gpa1-Gαq 嵌合蛋白触发 MAPK 通路，FUS1 启动子驱动 yEGFP/lacZ 表达，产生绿色荧光或蓝色显色。 双模式报告系统 项目

利用 pML104 载体表达 Cas9 与单靶点 sgRNA，通过 LiAc/PEG 化学转化入酵母，SD-Ura 营养缺陷平板筛选阳性克隆，并经菌落 PCR 与 Sanger 测序验证。当前进度：进行中，酶切失败后重建 sgRNA 载体。 02 报告体系构建——FUS1 驱动的双模式输出 目标：构建 pFUS1-yEGFP 与 pFUS1-lacZ 报告质粒，实现信号的可视化与定量检测。 以 pESC-HIS 为骨架，将 FUS1 启动子分别与 yEGFP 或 lacZ 报告基因连接。报告菌株接受上游 G 蛋白信号后启动转录：yEGFP 用于流式细胞术定量，lacZ 用于 X-Gal 染色定性。 03 Gpa1-Gα人源化——重

术定量，lacZ 用于 X-Gal 染色定性。 03 Gpa1-Gα人源化——重建人源 GPCR 信号偶联 目标：利用酿酒酵母同源重组机制，将 Gpa1 C 末端 KIGII 替换为人源 Gαq 的 EYNLV，实现 hM1Dq 与酵母 MAPK 通路的偶联。 线性整合片段结构为：500 bp 上游同源臂—人源化 Gpa1 突变序列—URA3 筛选盒—500 bp 下游同源臂。BY4741 为 ura3 营养缺陷型菌株，可通过 SD-Ura 平板筛选阳性整合克隆，最终经菌落 PCR 与 Sanger 测序确认替换。当前进度：待底盘敲除完成后进行。 04 PAGER识别融合蛋白——核心传感器元件的组装与表达 目标：完成 PAGER 融

PAGER识别融合蛋白——核心传感器元件的组装与表达 目标：完成 PAGER 融合蛋白基因的合成、大肠杆菌扩增与酵母转化，验证膜表面表达及抗原响应功能。 融合基因经酿酒酵母密码子优化后，两端添加 NdeI 与 BamHI 位点，全基因合成并克隆至 pGADT7（质粒编号 ABX63942）。通过 Top10 感受态细胞转化、质粒提取与双酶切验证确认构建正确：4 个阳性克隆质粒浓度为 408.45 / 404.85 / 297.15 / 355.90 ng/μL，A260/A280 ≈ 1.9，电泳条带与理论值（骨架 7939 bp，插入片段 2063 bp）一致。后续将通过 LiAc/PEG 转化入酵母，Western Blot 验

How We Got Here: From Wet-Cyclone Collection to a Cup of Glowing Medium This hardware began with a concrete observation. While reading up on how airborne bioaerosols are sampled, we came across the

aerosols are sampled, we came across the wet-cyclone principle: air is spun at high speed inside a chamber, aerosol particles are driven to the wall by centrifugal force, captured by a liquid film on that wall, and end up as liquid in a collection cup. The technique exists in order to collect what is in the air and han

er to collect what is in the air and hand it on for later analysis. We paused there. If the endpoint of collection is a cup of liquid anyway, why should that liquid only ever be water or buffer? If we replace the collection liquid with medium containing our yeast, sampling and detection can happen in the same cup. How

tection can happen in the same cup. How the process runs Following that thought, the whole process falls into eight steps: The device draws in air, and the cyclone spins airborne particles — including any influenza A virus present — into the liquid in the cup. That liquid is our engineered yeast culture, and the yeast

engineered yeast culture, and the yeast cells carry the PAGER fusion receptor on their surface, whose nanobody domain recognises the HA protein on the influenza A virion. When HA binds the nanobody, steric hindrance displaces the auto-inhibitory peptide MT1 from the hM1Dq receptor, relieving the receptor's self-inhibit

r, relieving the receptor's self-inhibition. In the presence of the agonist DCZ, which is already in the cup with the yeast before sampling starts, the de-repressed receptor activates the yeast MAPK pathway through the Gpa1–Gαq chimeric G protein, and the FUS1 promoter is switched on. FUS1 drives transcription of yEGFP

d on. FUS1 drives transcription of yEGFP, and the yeast begins to synthesise green fluorescent protein. We shine 485 nm excitation light into the sampling cup, exciting the fluorescent protein that has already been expressed. The fluorescent protein emits at 528 nm, collected by a receiver placed at 90° in space to the

a receiver placed at 90° in space to the excitation path. The receiver converts the optical signal into an electrical signal, and from that signal we judge whether influenza A virus is present in this air sample. The 90° angle is not arbitrary. The excitation beam is strong and the fluorescence is weak, and their centr

he fluorescence is weak, and their centre wavelengths differ by only about 43 nm. If the receiver sat on the same axis as the emitter, scattered excitation light would simply swamp the fluorescence. Turning it 90° takes the main excitation beam out of the receiver's direction, and two narrow-band filters then separate

d two narrow-band filters then separate that 43 nm properly. One more point is worth stating. DCZ sits in the same liquid as the yeast from before sampling begins, so the switch of this system is in practice thrown by HA alone: without HA the receptor stays self-inhibited and the pathway is closed, and only when HA is

pathway is closed, and only when HA is present is that inhibition relieved. DCZ effectively presets the switch to a state in which it can be opened, and the discriminating signal comes from the antigen itself. that usually breaks out during specific periods each year. Although the outbreak period is limited, influenza A imposes an extremely heavy global disease burden during each epidemic season. According to World Health Organization (WHO) reports, each year there are about 3–5 million severe cases and 290,000–650,000 influ

n severe cases and 290,000–650,000 influenza-related respiratory deaths. Influenza A does not originate in humans but comes from poultry, and influenza transmitted from poultry to humans has another name, “avian influenza”, such as “H5N1”. Avian influenza itself can only infect a small number of humans and cannot conti

small number of humans and cannot continue to spread from person to person, but it has undergone a terrifying change in pigs. This is because the respiratory tract of pigs carries both avian α-2,3 and human α-2,6 receptors. And by an unfortunate coincidence, when the same pig is infected with both avian influenza and

infected with both avian influenza and an already circulating human influenza, the eight RNA segments of the two viruses reshuffle and reassort, directly producing a completely new strain. The new strain may at once acquire the ability to recognize human receptors, to replicate in human cells and to spread from person

in human cells and to spread from person to person. Influenza A epidemics have a distinct cyclical character: after the peak of an epidemic, case numbers fall rapidly and public vigilance gradually fades; but by the next epidemic season, the mutated influenza A virus returns, once again threatening human health. We adopt action research, proposed by Kurt Lewin i

ction research, proposed by Kurt Lewin in 1946, as the theoretical framework for organizing our human practices, turning exchanges with external experts and partners into an iterable, traceable loop. What is action research Action research is a spiral-cycle method of “researching while doing, improving through research

SDG 3 first because the problem the project addresses is singular: influenza A outbreaks are discovered too late. Why influenza A deserves an earlier alarm Influenza A is good at hiding. Its reservoir sits in birds, and avian-origin strains typically infect only a few people and do not sustain human-to-human transmissi

do not sustain human-to-human transmission — until a variant appears that can. Its rhythm makes things worse. Cases surge every epidemic season, public attention fades once the season ends, and the next season a mutated influenza A returns — an enemy that knocks once a year, each time catching us off guard. time catching us off guard. Most existing detection only fires after the virus has flared up inside the body, which means every season we enter the game halfway through. The value of acting one step earlier is moving the moment of detection from "already outbreak" to "before it enters the body". The scale supports the

enters the body". The scale supports the same conclusion. WHO estimates that seasonal influenza causes roughly one billion infections worldwide every year, including 3–5 million severe cases and 290 000–650 000 respiratory deaths [2]. ded influenza pandemic and still dominates circulation in many regions: in Shenzhen CDC's 2024–2025 surveillance data compiled by our team, 83% of influenza-positive samples were typed as influenza A, with H1N1 predominant [4]. The three mainstream detection routes each carry a structural weakness. qRT-PCR is the most

tructural weakness. qRT-PCR is the most sensitive and quantitative — the accepted reference standard — but it requires laboratory equipment and trained staff and takes one to two hours. t of qPCR and it needs a reader and even longer handling time. Lateral-flow (colloidal gold) strips deliver an on-site result in 10–15 minutes without instruments, at the price of limited sensitivity, uncertain readings and frequent confirmatory retesting.
